results.reasoning: Driven in a terminal with the working tree's bin/walkdown.js on throwaway HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME machines; nothing was served, so no port was used. The five steps hold, through a pty and without one, and cart's row is unchanged throughout. n-0555 is fixed: the kept billing home imported from inside an unrelated ~/website is refused and shop's cart row is unchanged. Typed by the person, --project shop still moves cart there, as it should. The everyday cases hold: mv keeps every ID, delete and re-clone in place stays listed, re-clone elsewhere keeps the IDs, and a remote renamed in place stays listed. An unrelated repository at shop's deleted path is refused with guidance, and one at another path becomes its own project. A worktree and a second clone both answer already listed, never a new project. Switching ssh to https, or the fork workflow's upstream rename, then mv also keeps the IDs. Weighed edges, none filed: a GitHub rename with set-url, then mv or a re-clone elsewhere, gives a new project silently (about 3%: a rename is rare and two steps must follow). A shallow re-clone in place is refused with --project guidance (about 3%). A committed home only a second clone holds is refused as another project's label with no clone-aware hint (about 10%: two clones of one repository and a blueprint pulled into one of them).
